q-7589.name: Question 1
q-7589.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14275040/assets/e6aa1c1e19e5c46bb87f8268cbb34ef6316c74209b556e63bfd62a539be3b87f.png)

What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of the ellipse above?
q-7589.worked_solution:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-0.5,-6)$ and $(-0.5,2).$ So, the length of the major axis is $2-(-6)=8.$

The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-2,-2)$ and $(1,-2).$ So, the length of the minor axis is $1-(-2)=3.$

q-7589.html:
Question 1
?

What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of the ellipse above?

a
4 and 1.5
b
8 and 6
c
8 and 3
d
4 and 3
e
6 and 2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points (−0.5,−6) and (−0.5,2). So, the length of the major axis is 2−(−6)=8.

The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points (−2,−2) and (1,−2). So, the length of the minor axis is 1−(−2)=3.

What is the length of the semi-major axis of the ellipse given above?
q-7591.worked_solution:
The major axis is the longest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(2,1)$ and $(2,-4).$ So, the length of the major axis is $1-(-4)=5.$

The length of the semi-major axis is half the length of the major axis. So, the length of the semi-major axis is $\frac{5}{2}=2.5.$

What is the length of the semi-minor axis of the ellipse above?
q-70012.worked_solution:
The length of the semi-minor axis is half the length of the minor axis.

- The minor axis is the shortest diameter of the ellipse, which is the line segment bounded by the points $(-3,1)$ and $(1,1).$ So, the length of the minor axis is $1-(-3)=4.$

- The length of the semi-minor axis, then, is $\frac{4}{2}=2.$
